chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
You have not yet established brotherhood upon this matter, but rather you are being recognised upon it.

key_terms.تَعَارَفْتُمْ: you are being recognised/know each other

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between recognition and brotherhood in Shia Wilayah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) critiques the contemporary understanding of brotherhood, asserting that the current bond is merely based on mutual recognition of Wilayah rather than the profound spiritual unity (mukhabarah) expected of the faithful. This distinction highlights the transitional state of the Shia community during the Minor and Major Ghaibah, where allegiance to the Imams serves as the primary unifying factor before the ultimate establishment of divine brotherhood. The narration underscores that true cohesion requires not just shared belief in authority, but a deeper, intrinsic spiritual connection that is yet to be fully realized.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Hamza Bin Muhammad Al Tayyar, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:
‘You are not yet establishing brotherhood upon this matter (Al-Wilayah), but rather you are being recognised upon it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar from his father from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
You have not become brothers on the basis of this belief (of Shi’a Muslims) but you have recognized each other because of it.”’
